column5: Defines the specific, observable sponsorship behaviors expected of the Executive Sponsor and Steering Committee across the initiative lifecycle.
column6: Executive Sponsor (primary subject); Change Manager (facilitates); Steering Committee (co-signs)
column7: Signed at project kickoff; reviewed at every Phase Gate
column9: Prosci research shows active, visible sponsorship is the single largest predictor of change success; an unwritten expectation is an unenforceable one.
column10: A structured charter document naming specific actions (town halls attended, escalations resolved, communications sent) rather than a generic 'be supportive' commitment; tracked via the Sponsor-visibility tracker (Module 8).
column23: Operationalizes the Prosci Sponsor Model and Kotter Step 2 (Build a Guiding Coalition) as a signed, trackable commitment rather than prose guidance.

column5: Defines how Frontline Supervisors and People Managers involve their teams in decisions that affect them, rather than announcing decisions top-down.
column6: Frontline Supervisor / People Manager (primary subject); Change Manager (coaches); affected team (participants)
column7: Signed before Training & Change Readiness phase begins; practiced continuously through hypercare
column9: Resistance rooted in a 'done-to-me' perception of change is materially higher than resistance to a change the team helped shape, even in small ways.
column10: Structured participation moments (input sessions, pilot feedback loops, visible 'you said / we did' tracking) built into the Communication and Resistance Management macro processes.
column23: Extends Kotter Step 5 (Enable Action by Removing Barriers) to the supervisor layer; reduces role/will-based resistance surfaced in Module 11.

column5: Defines the message-audience-channel-timing discipline and the FAQ/reply-protocol standard every communication wave must follow.
column6: Change Manager / Communications Practitioner (primary subject); Executive Sponsor (co-signs key messages)
column7: Signed at communication-plan approval; enforced on every wave thereafter
column9: Ad hoc, inconsistent communication is a leading cause of the Awareness/Desire gap the Interaction Map's Exception E1 describes.
column10: A standing communication matrix (persona × channel × cadence), a mandatory FAQ reply-protocol SLA, and saturation checks (RULE-015) before any wave is scheduled.
column23: Operationalizes Kotter Step 4 (Communicate the Vision) as an enforceable standard rather than a plan document read once and shelved.

column5: Defines the methodology and sign-off standard for assessing how the change affects process, technology, role, location and professional identity.
column6: Change Manager (facilitates); Functional Process Owners (validate); Frontline Supervisors (confirm)
column7: Signed at Discovery & Design phase entry; re-validated at every major scope change
column9: An impact assessment done once, informally, and never revisited misses scope creep — the single most common cause of a stale stakeholder map.
column10: A required 5-dimension scoring rubric (RULE-005 human-confirmation gate), mandatory FPO/Supervisor validation sign-off, and a re-validation trigger on scope change.
column23: Formalizes Prosci Impact & Stakeholder Analysis as a governed, re-triggerable process rather than a one-time exercise.

column5: Defines the standard for group/team-level floor coaching delivered by People Managers during hypercare, distinct from individual 1:1 coaching.
column6: People Manager / Frontline Supervisor (primary subject); Change Manager (equips and audits)
column7: Signed before go-live; active throughout the hypercare window, tapering per MP-09 Task 4
column8: The production floor / work area, not a classroom
column9: Team-level regression is often visible on the floor days before it surfaces in individual metrics; a coaching standard catches it early.
column10: A defined cadence (e.g., daily floor walk during Week 1 of hypercare), a coaching-script standard (AIUC-11-assisted), and an escalation trigger to Change Manager if team-level metrics stall.
column23: Distinguishes team-level coaching (this charter) from CHTR-06 One-to-One Coaching, which handles individual identity-level concerns.

column5: Defines the standard for individual, identity-focused coaching conversations — most notably the divergence-case 1:1s described in Exception E2.
column6: Change Manager or trained People Manager (delivers); the individual employee (subject)
column7: Triggered on a confirmed Divergence Pattern case, a Desire score ≤2 with an unresolved barrier, or an employee self-request
column8: A private, confidential setting — never the open floor
column9: Group coaching cannot address a genuine identity/loss concern; conflating the two risks minimizing what an individual is actually experiencing.
column10: A structured 1:1 protocol (confirm the concern → distinguish loss from reluctance → provide closure if a genuine loss is identified → re-check Bridges only, not Knowledge/Ability) with mandatory Qualitative Coding Workbench logging.
column23: Directly operationalizes the Framework Interaction Map's Exception E2 recovery workflow as a formal, signed coaching standard rather than ad hoc practice.

column5: Defines the three-stage progressive mentoring model (Trainee, Observer, Autonomous) that carries an individual from initial training through to independent, unsupervised competence.
column6: Trainer / designated Mentor (delivers); the mentee (subject); Functional Process Owner (validates competency gates)
column7: Begins at Training & Change Readiness phase; each stage transition is a gated event, not a calendar milestone
column8: Sandbox environment (Trainee), live environment under observation (Observer), live environment unsupervised (Autonomous)
column9: 'Trained' and 'capable' are not the same thing — Module 10 explicitly separates attendance from demonstrated competency; a single training event rarely produces autonomous performance.
column10: A four-part sub-process — Diagnosis (assess starting Knowledge/Ability) → Training Plan Elaboration (design the stage-gated path) → Execution (deliver each stage with explicit entry/exit criteria) → Closure (formal Autonomous sign-off) — see D31a for the full task/step mapping and D31c for the three-stage model itself.
column23: The one charter whose actions span the widest range of tasks/steps — from MP-05 Task 1 (curriculum design) through Task 5 (remediation) — because mentoring is a full-lifecycle discipline, not a single event.

column5: Defines the cadence, instrument standard and consent protocol for every structured pulse survey, rapid pulse, and 1:1 interview used to capture readiness signals.
column7: Baseline at project start; recurring at every Phase Gate; rapid pulses around high-anxiety moments (go-live)
column8: Survey platform (structured pulses), floor/desk (rapid pulses), private setting (interviews)
column9: An inconsistent or overly frequent pulse cadence produces survey fatigue and degrades response quality exactly when the signal matters most (around go-live).
column10: A fixed instrument library (baseline, phase-gate, rapid, interview guide), a maximum-frequency rule per population (ties to RULE-015 saturation logic), and mandatory consolidation into the Composite Readiness Index within a defined SLA.
column23: Standardizes the instruments referenced throughout Module 6/7 and the worked Survey Form exception-handling example (D02 TASK-0701-WORKED) under one governing charter.
